newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Argentina takes its Mercosur complaints to Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Argentina takes its Mercosur complaints to Brazil.

text.p: Argentine officials, upset over Brazil's delays in implementing Mercosur rules, have arrived in Brasilia to air a laundry list of complaints ranging from export subsidies to financial restrictions, diplomats said.

Argentina's Trade, Industry and Mining Secretary Alieto Guadagni and International Economic Relations Secretary Jorge Campbell met with high-level Brazilian officials prior to this week's Mercosur executive board meeting.

Argentina's complaints include Brazil's delays in implementing Mercosur norms, caps on growth of foreign bank subsidiaries, bans on subsidized corn and rice imports and restrictions on Argentine firms bidding on public works projects.

Buenos Aires is also griping about the reluctance of Brazilian banks to buy Argentine pesos, obstacles placed by state oil firm Petrobras on imports of Argentine oil products and delays in issuing import rules.
A foreign ministry spokesman said the Brazilian government had no immediate response to the complaints.
Despite trade disputes between its two largest members, the success of Mercosur has prompted Chile and members of the five-nation Andean Pact to seek free trade agreements with the union.

Mercosur's executive board also is expected to meet with Bolivian officials to put the finishing touches on a free trade accord and set dates next week to meet with representatives from the Andean group.
Alarm bells were set off in Buenos Aires last month when Brazil, Argentina's largest trading partner, released August trade figures.
It showed Brazilian exports to Argentina jumped 41.5 percent to $520.2 million compared with the same month last year, virtually wiping out its trade surplus with Brazil.

Meanwhile, the Mercosur board is likely to take up the sensitive issue of auto imports, the subject of a heated dispute last year between Argentina and Brazil, as well as a proposal to establish a Mercosur Development Bank.
